title: Before & After School Site Director at Creslane Elementary
description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

When you join Champions, you’ll be supporting hardworking families and elementary-aged kids during out-of-school time, on school grounds. Whether you’re partnering with administrators to bring our programs to their district, or buddying up with students to aim higher, think bigger, and never give up, you’ll be leading the way toward inspired learning.

If you’re passionate about inspiring children and teachers alike to learn and grow, the Site Director role could be for you! Site Directors are passionate about educational excellence and empowering confident teachers. As a Site Director, you will use our nationally recognized curriculum as a framework to create unique and engaging classroom experiences. Site Directors are committed to making their site successful and know that important relationships with children, families, and their team are critical to success. Successful Site Directors are fully engaged, enthusiastic about their work, and eager to share their knowledge.

When you join our team as a Site Director, you will:

  • Lead and supervise a group of teachers to create unique and engaging classroom experiences, leverage and develop “best in class” educators to be passionate and committed professionals
  • Ensure your site is operating effectively; maintain licensing, safety, and educational standards
  • Partner with parents with a shared desire to provide the best care and education for their children
  • Cultivate positive relationships with families, teachers, school and district leaders, state licensing authorities, community contacts, and corporate partners
  • Lead recruitment and enrollment efforts of new families and children in our sites

Required Skills and Experience:

  • At least one year of teaching experience with the ability to develop, engage, and inspire a team
  • A love for children and a strong desire to make a difference every day
  • Ability to build relationships with families and staff and create a dynamic environment where play and discovery go hand-in-hand
  • Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, multi-task and manage multiple situations effectively
  • Meet state specific guidelines for the role
  • Be physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40 pounds, and work indoors or outdoors. Be able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity
  • Read, write, understand, and speak English to communicate with children and their parents in English

Our benefits meet you where you are. We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life:
- Know your whole family is supported with discounted child care benefits.

- Breathe easy with medical, dental, and vision benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
- Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with employee assistance programs.
- Feel great and thrive with access to health and wellness programs, paid time off and discounts for work necessities, such as cell phones.
- … and much more.


We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.

title: HW & SW Engineering Application Admins
description:
​Technical Lead, IT Solutions
Req ID: 137499
Remote Position: Hybrid
Hiring Manager: Paul Stanners
Band: 10
Region: Asia
Country: Malaysia
State/Province: Bayan Lepas
City: Penang

Summary


We are seeking a highly technical, execution-focused Hardware & Software Engineering Applications System Administrator (Band 10) to support the core engineering applications environment for the Hardware Platform Solutions (HPS) group. The System Administrator is responsible for the direct operational and technical execution of the daily installation, packaging, configuration, and troubleshooting of specialized R&D application toolchains.

The successful candidate will provide disciplined operational support across 12 global Design Centers to eliminate engineering environment blocks and optimize developer productivity. This role requires an agile approach to manage the rapid iteration and specialized tools necessary for high-performance product development, directly executing provisioning workflows that accelerate engineering velocity and eliminate onboarding productivity gaps.

Core Responsibilities


1. Hands-on Application Operations & New Hire Enablement

• Execute Onboarding Provisioning: Implement and run automated application provisioning playbooks to eliminate the traditional "Day 1 productivity gap," ensuring new software and hardware engineers are immediately equipped with specialized toolsets.

• Technical Tool Maintenance: Manage the daily installation, configuration, application packaging, and technical integration of specialized R&D software across physical lab systems and cloud-based engineering workstations.

• Day-to-Day Engineering Support: Serve as the direct, hands-on technical bridge between corporate IT infrastructure and engineering teams, resolving environment blocks and optimizing execution workflows.

2. Hardware Engineering Toolchain & License Administration

• EDA and CAD Deployment: Execute application packaging, license tracking, and configuration management for the multi-disciplinary HPS hardware engineering application environment.

• Hands-on Toolchain Maintenance: Provide direct administrative and technical troubleshooting support for specialized hardware engineering environments, ensuring high availability for the following application suites:

• Mechanical & Thermal: PTC Creo, Windchill PLM/Reliability, SolidWorks, Simcenter FloTHERM, and Cadence Celsius EC.

• Electrical & Power: Cadence OrCAD Capture, ConceptHDL, Synopsys HSPICE, and Ansys Electronics.

• Signal/Power Integrity (SI/PI): Cadence Sigrity, Agilent ADS, HyperLynx, and Keysight SystemVue.

• PCBA Layout & Logic/FPGA: Cadence Allegro PCB Designer, Altium, Valor NPI, Siemens QuestaSim, AMD Vivado, Altera Quartus, and Lattice Diamond.

• Optics & Photonics: COMSOL, Lumerical, Optiwave, VPIphotonics, and Zemax.

• License Server Operations: Administer and monitor central concurrent-user license managers, handling license queuing configurations and multi-tenant tracking utilities.

3. Software Engineering, DevOps, & Lab Test Support

• ALM & DevOps Support: Provide direct operational support for application lifecycle management (ALM), source control, and container platforms utilizing Azure DevOps, Jira Cloud Enterprise, Confluence Cloud Premium, Git, GitKraken, Docker, and Kubernetes.

• Firmware & Secure Development Lifecycle: Administer specialized secure code compilation and vulnerability environments, handling AMI BIOS/BMC source code toolchains, Green Hills MULTI compilers, Black Duck, Coverity, Opswat MetaDefender, and Defensics.

• Validation & Lab Synchronization: Manage the local deployment, active licensing, and update synchronization for specialized validation and lab testing software, including Ixia (IxNetwork), Spirent Test Center, Wireshark, LabVIEW, TestStand, and hardware debugger IDEs (SEGGER J-Link, TI Code Composer, ARM Keil).

Knowledge/Skills/Competencies


Required Technical Skills

• Hands-on Engineering Tool Competency: Direct technical experience installing, patching, configuring, and deploying major EDA/CAD suites (such as Cadence, Synopsys, Ansys, or PTC).

• DevOps & Infrastructure Skills: Practical administrative experience managing Azure DevOps, Jira, Git repositories, CI/CD pipelines, and containerization systems (Docker/Kubernetes).

• License Architecture Knowledge: Functional knowledge of working with FlexLM, RMS, and similar vendor-specific license management server environments.

• Cross-Platform OS Familiarity: Technical comfort supporting Windows desktop applications alongside non-standard Linux base development images (Ubuntu, Rocky Linux) and enterprise endpoint configurations (BigFix, ThreatLocker).

Strongly Preferred Certifications

• CompTIA Linux+, Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA), or Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate

• Azure DevOps Engineer Expert or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional

• Certified Jira System Administrator

Soft Skills & Working Style

• Detailed Documentation: Proven ability to generate flawless application installation playbooks, precise packaging documentation, and clear troubleshooting scripts.

• Tactical Problem Solver: Exceptional technical troubleshooting skills, capable of identifying workarounds and diagnosing complex engineering application bugs within highly secure enterprise environments.

• Cross-functional Partner: Strong communication skills to interact directly and efficiently with HPS Design Center engineers, project managers, and global infrastructure tier-3 teams.

• Resource Optimization: Highly organized approach to tracking local software licensing utilization, preventing downtime, and advising management on upcoming software capacity or maintenance renewals.

Physical Demands


• Duties of this position are performed in a normal office environment.

• Duties may require extended periods of sitting and sustained visual concentration on a computer monitor or on numbers and other detailed data. Repetitive manual movements (e.g., data entry, using a computer mouse, using a calculator, etc.) are frequently required.

Education & Experience


• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Minimum of 5+ years of hands-on experience in enterprise IT system administration or application engineering, with at least 2+ years explicitly focused on supporting an active R&D engineering team.

Notes


This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities of the position. Employees are held accountable for all duties of the job. Job duties and the % of time identified for any function are subject to change at any time.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on any protected status (including race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran or disability status or other characteristics protected by law).

title: Associate Producer - Live & Broadcast Events
description:
How You’ll Contribute:
We are seeking a motivated, organized, and technically curious Associate Producer to support the planning, coordination, and execution of live, virtual, hybrid, and broadcast productions.
Working closely with the Executive Producer and an established production team, this individual will assist with all phases of production, including project intake, production planning, asset coordination, rehearsals, live event execution, and post-production follow-up.
This is an early-career production position designed for an individual with foundational experience in professional production environments who is eager to develop their skills and grow within an established organization.
The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience supporting live events, virtual productions, or broadcast workflows, along with strong communication skills, attention to detail, and a willingness to learn established production processes.
While previous experience in television or broadcast production is highly valued, we are equally interested in candidates who demonstrate strong production fundamentals, technical aptitude, adaptability, and professional growth potential.

Work Environment & Schedule

This position is based in Santa Clara, California.
Onsite presence is required for live productions, studio operations, rehearsals, and event preparation.
Some remote flexibility may be available when supporting virtual productions.
Schedule flexibility may be required to accommodate live events, rehearsals, and occasional productions outside standard business hours.
The Associate Producer will work under the guidance of the Executive Producer and established production leadership, with opportunities for increasing responsibility as skills and experience develop.

What You’ll Do:

Production Planning & Coordination

Support the Executive Producer and production team in planning and executing live, virtual, hybrid, and broadcast productions.
Assist with project intake, scope definition, requirements gathering, and production scheduling.
Develop and maintain production timelines, run-of-show documents, rehearsal schedules, production checklists, and event documentation.
Coordinate production logistics, resources, and deliverables across internal teams and external partners.
Track production milestones, outstanding action items, and changes to production requirements.
Support pre-production meetings, rehearsals, production execution, and post-event reviews.
Take increasing ownership of assigned production tasks and smaller productions as experience and proficiency develop.

Live, Virtual & Hybrid Production Support

Assist with the execution of live in-person events, virtual productions, and hybrid events involving both onsite and remote participants.
Support Zoom Meetings and Zoom Webinars, including multiple presenters, remote participants, presentation content, video playback, and graphics.

title: Assistant Director at Del Mar Highlands KinderCare
description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

Our teachers, center staff, and field leaders are the heart and soul of our business. When you join us, you’ll be directly supporting children and their education every day and experiencing the trials and triumphs that come with that responsibility. But you’ll never be alone. You’ll do it all with a village of dedicated and passionate humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do. The best part? Seeing the positive impact you’re making on the lives of young learners and their families—and knowing that your work matters.

If you’re passionate about positively impacting the lives of others and making waves in the world of early childhood education, the Assistant Director role might be for you! Assistant Directors play an integral role in leading our centers to success. With KinderCare’s world-class curriculum, center accreditation process, and passionate teaching staff, together, our Assistant Directors and Center Directors are changing the world one achievement at a time. As an Assistant Director, you will educate parents, teachers, and leaders on the value of early childhood education and make that value come to life for the children in your center.

When you join our team as an Assistant Center Director, you will:

  • Assist the Center Director in leading teaching staff, supporting families, and achieving enrollment, accreditation, and operational objectives
  • Partner with parents with a shared desire to provide the best care and education for their children
  • Cultivate positive relationships with families, teachers, state licensing authorities, community contacts, and corporate partners
  • Serve in various roles throughout the center as needed, including teacher, cook, and/or driver.

Skills, Education, and Experience:

  • At least two years of early childhood education experience required, with an understanding of developmentally appropriate practices and the ability to ensure its use in the classroom
  • Excellent administrative, organizational, verbal, listening, and communication skills required
  • CPR and First Aid Certification or willingness to obtain
  • Meet state specific guidelines for the role
  • Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40 pounds, and work indoors or outdoors
  • Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity
  • Read, write, understand, and speak English to communicate with children and their parents in English
  • Please indicate if you require reasonable accommodation to perform the essential functions of the job
Range of pay $25.60 - $29.85 Hourly

Our benefits meet you where you are. We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life:
- Know your whole family is supported with discounted child care benefits. - Breathe easy with medical, dental, and vision benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
- Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with employee assistance programs.
- Feel great and thrive with access to health and wellness programs, paid time off and discounts for work necessities, such as cell phones.
- … and much more.


We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

title: [Corporate] IT Support Engineer
description:
We are looking for a customer-oriented and experienced IT Support Engineer (L1) to join our Corporate IT team. This role is based in our Taipei office and provides support to internal users across multiple office locations.

As a first-line IT support contact, you will provide on-site and remote support through ITSM. You will assist users with endpoint devices, identity and access management, collaboration tools, network connectivity, video-conferencing equipment, and other day-to-day IT service needs.

We expect you to independently resolve most standard first-line issues. For complex, high-impact, or high-risk cases, you will provide clear diagnostic information, escalate through the appropriate process, and maintain ticket follow-up and user communication.

Responsibilities:

User and Technical Support:

  • Handle IT incidents and service requests through ITSM, walk-in support, and approved remote-support channels.
  • Provide first-line support and troubleshooting for macOS, Windows, laptops, mobile devices, printers, scanners, and common peripherals.
  • Support the day-to-day use and basic troubleshooting of enterprise collaboration, productivity, identity and access management, and endpoint-related tools.
  • Assist with common user-side issues involving sign-in, access, MFA, devices, and network connectivity.
  • Categorize, prioritize, document, track, and escalate tickets based on business impact, urgency, and established procedures.
  • Escalate complex, high-impact, security-related, or out-of-scope issues to the appropriate technical teams while maintaining ticket follow-up and user communication.

Office and Meeting Room Support:

  • Support the daily use, checks, and troubleshooting of office automation, video-conferencing, and meeting room equipment.
  • Help ensure equipment and connectivity are ready before important meetings and provide on-site support when required.

Asset and Employee Lifecycle Support:

  • Assist with IT asset receiving, tagging, inventory checks, deployment, collection, and related record maintenance.
  • Support IT processes for employee onboarding, offboarding, and role changes, including device preparation, recovery, and coordination of account or access requests.

Knowledge, AI, and Service Improvement:

  • Maintain FAQs, knowledge base articles, and standard operating procedures (SOPs). Convert frequent or recurring issues into reusable solutions to improve self-service and team efficiency.
  • Use company-approved generative AI tools to assist with troubleshooting research, ticket summarization, knowledge discovery, user response drafting, and documentation drafts.
  • Validate AI-generated content for technical accuracy, procedural alignment, and information security considerations before sharing it with users or incorporating it into official documentation.
  • Provide first-line support for basic sign-in, access, and general use issues involving company-approved AI productivity and developer assistance tools. Escalate matters involving system administration, integrations, data protection, or security risks through established processes.
  • Follow company policies for information security, data protection, account management, and responsible AI use.

Requirements

Requirements:

  • 2+ years of experience in IT Service Desk, Help Desk, Desktop Support, Corporate IT Support, or a similar first-line IT support role.
  • Ability to independently resolve most common L1 IT issues and determine appropriate escalation timing and resolver teams.
  • Familiarity with day-to-day support and troubleshooting for macOS and Windows.
  • Practical experience supporting enterprise collaboration, productivity, identity and access management, or endpoint tools.
  • First-line troubleshooting knowledge of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, Wi-Fi, and wired network connectivity.
  • Experience using an ITSM platform to manage tickets.
  • Strong customer service mindset, communication, problem-solving, and documentation skills.
  • Foundational understanding of information security, including MFA, account and access management, endpoint security, phishing awareness, and data protection.
  • Experience using generative AI tools for troubleshooting research, documentation, or productivity improvement. Able to assess whether AI-generated output is appropriate and complete the required human review and validation in accordance with company data protection requirements.
  • Strong written communication skills in both Chinese and English, with the ability to support English-language tickets and basic remote communication across offices.

Preferred Qualification:

  • Familiarity with Jira Service Management (JSM) features such as SLA management, Knowledge Base, Assets, or Automation.
  • Experience supporting enterprise collaboration, identity and access management, endpoint, or video-conferencing systems.
  • Experience with IT asset management, device lifecycle management, and employee onboarding/offboarding processes.
  • Basic automation or scripting skills in PowerShell, Python, Shell Script, or similar technologies.
  • ITIL Foundation certification, experience with entry-level security incident handling, or experience improving AI-assisted knowledge management, service process automation, or self-service capabilities is a plus.

description:
Job Description

The future of money is being built right now. At FIS, we help the world’s businesses, banks and communities move, manage, and grow money with confidence. Join a team that values fresh thinking, works together to solve complex challenges, and creates technology that powers everyday life.

About the Role

The Program Manager Principal is a strategic leadership role responsible for driving complex, enterprise-wide programs that support critical business objectives across FIS Capital Markets. This highly visible position requires strong executive presence, exceptional stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence decision-making at senior leadership levels. You will lead cross-functional teams, manage large-scale program initiatives, and ensure successful delivery through strategic planning, governance, risk management, and execution excellence.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute enterprise program strategies aligned to business priorities, establishing program governance, objectives, resource plans, and measurable outcomes.
  • Lead cross-functional and geographically distributed teams to deliver complex initiatives within scope, budget, quality, and timeline expectations.
  • Build and manage executive stakeholder relationships, providing strategic guidance, transparent communication, and actionable program reporting.
  • Identify and mitigate risks, dependencies, and constraints while driving continuous improvement and operational excellence across multiple workstreams.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in securities, capital markets, investment services, brokerage, clearing, custody, or related financial services industries.
  • Proven success leading large-scale, enterprise programs and strategic initiatives within complex, highly regulated environments.
  • Demonstrated executive presence with the ability to influence senior leaders, clients, and key stakeholders through effective communication and leadership.
  • Strong strategic thinking, business acumen, and expertise in program governance, risk management, budgeting, and resource planning.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in Business, Finance, Technology, or a related field.
  • Experience leading transformation, modernization, or strategic change initiatives within capital markets organizations.
  • PgMP, PMP, or other relevant program management certification.

The impact you’ll make

As a Program Manager Principal, you will play a critical role in shaping and delivering strategic initiatives that drive business growth, operational excellence, and client success. Your leadership will help align teams, strengthen execution, and influence organizational decision-making. By bringing a strategic outlook and deep capital markets expertise, you will help ensure programs deliver meaningful outcomes that support the future direction of the business.

When you join FIS, you become part of a team that's shaping how the world pays, banks, and invests. We're committed to helping you thrive, both professionally and personally.

At FIS, we offer you:

description:

Our teachers, center staff, and field leaders are the heart and soul of our business. When you join us, you’ll be directly supporting children and their education every day and experiencing the trials and triumphs that come with that responsibility. But you’ll never be alone. Seeing the positive impact you’re making on the lives of young learners and their families—and knowing that your work matters.

Education Directors educate parents, teachers, and community leaders on the incredible value of early childhood education and make that value come to life for the children in their center.

When you join our team as a Education Director, you will:

  • Develop and train a team of educators to be passionate and committed to teaching KLC's curriculum
  • Partner with parents with a shared desire to provide the best care and education for their children
  • Cultivate positive relationships with families, teachers, state licensing authorities, community contacts, and corporate partners
  • Tap into your expertise in education to grow KinderCare Learning Companies' presence in the community, leading to the growth of new families and children in our centers based on the growing need for world class education.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • At least one year of solid leadership experience with the ability to develop, engage, and inspire a team
  • A love for children and a strong desire to make a difference every day
  • Ability to build relationships with families and staff and create a dynamic environment where play and discovery go hand-in-hand
  • Apply outside knowledge and resources to provide creative solutions within the education field; partner with inclusion services where learning challenges may be present with a child.
  • Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and the ability to multi-task and manage multiple situations effectively including monthly meetings with parents on where their child is progressing

  • Ability to physically use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40 pounds, and work indoors or outdoors. Ability to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity with children.
  • Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents

Range of pay $56,250.00 - $102,250.00 Salary

title: Memory Care Director
company: Western States Lodging, Management and Development
description:
Bridgewater by Legacy Retirement Communities
Memory Care Director | Lead with Compassion. Create Connection.
BridgeWater is a beautiful new Legacy Retirement Community experiencing continued occupancy growth as more residents choose to make the community their home. Because of this exciting growth, we're expanding our clinical team and are looking for a compassionate, experienced Memory Care Director to provide exceptional care to our growing family. Our Memory Care Director provides leadership and oversight for the daily operations of the Memory Care neighborhood, ensuring residents living with Alzheimer’s disease, dementia, and other forms of memory loss receive exceptional, person-centered care in a safe, engaging, and supportive environment.
This position independently manages day-to-day Memory Care operations, leads and develops associates, oversees staffing and scheduling, supports resident service planning, maintains regulatory compliance, and partners closely with residents, families, and community leadership. The Memory Care Director serves as a trusted resource for associates and families while helping create an environment where residents are known, valued, and supported according to their individual needs and preferences.
What’s in it for you- Compensation & Benefits

Competitive Pay - hourly.

The starting rate is based on experience and qualifications. This position participates in our compensation program, which provides opportunities for future pay growth based on performance and career development.

401(k) with a dollar-for-dollar company match up to 4%
Hotel discounts at select Western States Lodging & Management properties

Eligible full-time associates are entitled to the following:

Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans plus Health Savings Account (HSA) options

Optional supplemental benefits, including accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and other coverage options.

Personal Time Off (PTO) and Vacation benefits

What You'll Do

Independently oversee the daily operations of the Memory Care neighborhood while maintaining high standards of resident care, safety, service, and engagement.
Lead, schedule, train, coach, and develop Memory Care associates while promoting accountability and teamwork.
Ensure appropriate staffing levels and coordinate scheduling and coverage based on resident needs and operational requirements.
Foster a resident-centered environment that promotes dignity, independence, respect, privacy, choice, and meaningful engagement.
Participate in resident assessments and oversee the development, implementation, and ongoing review of individualized resident service plans.
Ensure associates understand and consistently follow resident service plans and established care practices.
Monitor changes in resident needs, behaviors, preferences, and abilities and coordinate appropriate communication and follow-up.
Build strong relationships with residents and families, providing regular communication and addressing questions or concerns professionally and compassionately.
Lead associate onboarding, training, coaching, performance feedback, and professional development within the department.
Support recruitment, retention, associate engagement, and succession planning efforts for the Memory Care team.
Ensure compliance with applicable state and federal regulations, company policies, community standards, and Memory Care requirements.
Maintain accurate documentation and department records while protecting resident confidentiality and rights.
Participate in quality assurance and performance improvement initiatives and implement corrective actions when needed.

What Makes You Successful

Current Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) certification, as required by the community or applicable regulations.
Current CPR certification.
Previous leadership or supervisory experience in senior living, memory care, assisted living, long-term care, or a related healthcare setting preferred.
A compassionate and confident leader with a passion for serving seniors and individuals experiencing memory loss.
Previous experience in memory care, assisted living, long-term care, or a similar senior living environment.
Previous supervisory or management experience leading direct-care associates.
Working knowledge of Alzheimer’s disease, dementia, and person-centered memory care practices.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to coach, develop, motivate, and hold associates accountable.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills with residents, families, associates, and healthcare professionals.

You Know You're Successful When...
Residents receive consistent, individualized care and feel safe, respected, engaged, and valued. Families trust the Memory Care team and feel informed and supported throughout their loved one’s experience. The department maintains strong staffing, documentation, regulatory compliance, and service standards while creating a warm and welcoming environment residents are proud to call home.
Why Join Western States Lodging & Management?
Western States Lodging & Management is a leading property management company with a diverse portfolio that includes nationally recognized hotel brands such as Hilton, Marriott, and IHG, Legacy Senior Living communities, and Nxt multifamily apartment communities throughout the western United States.
Our mission is simple: Serving You Like Family. That commitment extends beyond our guests and residents—it defines how we treat our associates and business partners. We believe that great people build great communities, which is why we invest in our team through meaningful work, ongoing professional development, and opportunities for long-term career growth. At Western States Lodging & Management, we encourage every team member to serve as an Ambassador of our values, a trusted Consultant who brings knowledge and solutions, a Collaborator who builds strong relationships through teamwork, and a Coach who is passionate and empowers others to learn, grow, and succeed.
Whether you're launching your career or bringing years of experience, you'll find a workplace where your contributions are valued, your ideas are welcomed, and your potential is supported every step of the way.
Apply today and discover why thousands of associates have chosen Western States as the place to build a meaningful career.

title: Bioprocess Specialist, Downstream
description:
Scope of Function:


The Bioprocess Specialist I position reports to the Downstream Manufacturing Supervisor.

Bioprocess Specialist I shall perform the production process under cGMP ensuring adherence to safety protocols and quality standards. This role is responsible for supporting the overall Downstream GMP process through the application of broad knowledge of theories and principles. They will perform operational and routine tasks in the production of bulk biologics from harvest of cell culture systems through column chromatography, tangential flow filtration and viral filtration to bulk drug substance for Phase 1/2/3 and commercial cGMP manufacturing. They will document all work performed following ALCOA+ principles.

Specific Duties:


• Operates pharmaceutical manufacturing equipment such as single use mixers, depth filtration skids, TFF skids, chromatography skids and in-process testing equipment.

• Executes all Downstream Clinical Manufacturing and Development operations, including but not limited to work functions in buffer preparation, chromatography execution, pre-viral and viral clearance, and technology transfer to manufacturing.

• Collaborate with colleagues and supervisors to troubleshoot and resolve issues in a timely manner.

• Demonstrates, understands, and adheres to Goodwin Biotechnology policies, GMP standards and safety procedures.

• Performs and monitors critical processes, executes manufacturing batch records (MBR) for specific projects to manufacture cell-derived biopharmaceuticals in compliance with cGMP guidelines and regulations.

• Perform routine maintenance and cleaning of production equipment.

• Accurately document and record production data and activities according to ALCOA+.

• Inform supervisor/manager on progress of projects, transfer data, process details, etc.

• Supports the development of batch records, SOP's and protocols as required.

• Supports Goodwin Biotechnology QA during audits and regulatory inspections.

• Participate in training and continuing education to stay current with industry developments and regulations.

• Adhere to safety protocols and maintain a clean and organized work environment.

• Follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs) to maintain compliance with regulations

• Supports other manufacturing processes teams and other GBI groups as necessary to achieve manufacturing goals and objectives.


This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

Our teachers, center staff, and field leaders are the heart and soul of our business. When you join us, you’ll be directly supporting children and their education every day and experiencing the trials and triumphs that come with that responsibility. But you’ll never be alone. You’ll do it all with a village of dedicated and passionate humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do. The best part? Seeing the positive impact you’re making on the lives of young learners and their families—and knowing that your work matters.

If you’re passionate about positively impacting the lives of others and making waves in the world of early childhood education, the Assistant Director role might be for you! Assistant Directors play an integral role in leading our centers to success. With KinderCare’s world-class curriculum, center accreditation process, and passionate teaching staff, together, our Assistant Directors and Center Directors are changing the world one achievement at a time. As an Assistant Director, you will educate parents, teachers, and leaders on the value of early childhood education and make that value come to life for the children in your center.

When you join our team as an Assistant Center Director, you will:

  • Assist the Center Director in leading teaching staff, supporting families, and achieving enrollment, accreditation, and operational objectives
  • Partner with parents with a shared desire to provide the best care and education for their children
  • Cultivate positive relationships with families, teachers, state licensing authorities, community contacts, and corporate partners
  • Serve in various roles throughout the center as needed, including teacher, cook, and/or driver.

Skills, Education, and Experience:

  • At least two years of early childhood education experience required, with an understanding of developmentally appropriate practices and the ability to ensure its use in the classroom
  • Excellent administrative, organizational, verbal, listening, and communication skills required
  • CPR and First Aid Certification or willingness to obtain
  • Meet state specific guidelines for the role
  • Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40 pounds, and work indoors or outdoors
  • Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity
  • Read, write, understand, and speak English to communicate with children and their parents in English
  • Please indicate if you require reasonable accommodation to perform the essential functions of the job

In the state of Minnesota, we currently provide an additional $3.00 per hour premium on all classroom hours worked in addition to the range of pay listed. This premium is funded through the Minnesota Great Start Grant Compensation Support Program.


Range of pay $20.25 - $23.60 Hourly

Our benefits meet you where you are. We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life:
- Know your whole family is supported with discounted child care benefits. - Breathe easy with medical, dental, and vision benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
- Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with employee assistance programs.
- Feel great and thrive with access to health and wellness programs, paid time off and discounts for work necessities, such as cell phones.
- … and much more.


We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.


In the state of Illinois, we currently provide a 15% premium in addition to the range of pay listed to all hourly employees working in a center that participates in the Illinois Smart Start Workforce Grant.

KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.

title: Staff Product Development
description:
Staff Product Line Manager

Job Summary:
The Staff Product Line Manager serves as a senior technical and strategic partner within the Warfighter Systems business, owning a major product group and driving its multi‑year roadmap, technology integration, and market direction. This role expands beyond product‑specific execution to influence cross‑product architectural decisions, investment priorities, and long‑term capability evolution.
The successful candidate will be a subject matter expert in night vision technologies, imaging sensors, optical systems, soldier‑borne systems, and networked battlefield architectures. They will translate customer needs, operational use cases, and mission requirements into actionable product strategies, requirements, and business cases. This role requires strong communication, technical depth, and the ability to influence engineering, operations, BD, and senior leadership. While not a people-management role, it is a high‑impact leadership position.
Responsibilities and Tasks:
Product Strategy & Roadmap Leadership

Own the strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle for one or more product groups within Warfighter Systems.
Develop multi‑year product strategies informed by customer needs, market assessments, and technology trends.
Facilitate product trade studies and define feature prioritization for next‑generation night vision and soldier‑borne capabilities.
Create business cases for product investments, including IRAD justification, ROI assessments, and value‑based pricing strategies.
Ensure alignment of product‑level roadmaps to the broader Warfighter Systems portfolio.

Customer Advocacy & Requirements Leadership

Act as a senior customer advocate - capturing requirements, operational use cases, and CONOPS and translating them into clear technical requirements.
Lead customer technical interactions, product demonstrations, prototype planning, and requirement validation activities.
Author and socialize product‑offering requirements and supporting documentation across engineering, BD, PM, and operations.

Cross‑Functional Influence & Technical Direction

Provide technical guidance to engineering teams in guiding component and architecture selections consistent with market and other key requirements.
Work with cross-functional leaders to shape development priorities, investment decisions, and technology integration paths.
Partner with PEM to lead or support major product checkpoint reviews, ensuring designs meet cost, schedule, performance, and user‑driven requirements.
Establish and maintain DTUPC targets and coordinate with engineering and operations to achieve cost‑performance objectives.
Assess competitive strategies/position, emerging technologies, and market shifts to guide product evolution.

Architecture, Technology, and Systems Integration Support

Support system-level architectural decisions that span multiple products.
Provide technology assessments and integrate findings into product strategies and roadmaps.
Contribute to cross‑product system concepts, including integrated night vision, soldier power, tactical radios, shared situational awareness, AR displays, and networked sensor systems.
Help ensure technical cohesion and interoperability across the Warfighter Systems product family.

Execution Support & Development Oversight

Monitor all development activities for assigned product lines, identifying risks and aligning priorities with strategic objectives.
Collaborate with program management on schedule, cost, and engineering deliverables.
Support proposal development, customer reviews, and internal strategy reviews.
Provide input into IRAD and EAID rationalization for related technologies and product lines.

Customer Engagement & Growth

Engage regularly with domestic and international customers to strengthen relationships and identify opportunities for product and capability growth.
Deliver technical briefs and support BD capture activities with grounded technical insight.
Support prototype demonstrations and align them with the product strategy and BD capture plans.
Author and socialize white papers and product/technology briefings developed to influence or define potential CRAD projects, CRADA relationships, or other collaborative constructs with customers.

Collaboration Across TSDEF

Work with other TSDEF business units to leverage technologies that enhance Warfighter Systems product offerings.
Participate in enterprise‑level technology discussions when relevant, contributing product‑level insights to broader architectural initiatives.

Travel Requirement:

Approximately 25% travel to TSDEF sites, trade shows, and customer locations worldwide.

Education, Experience & Certification Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, systems engineering, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of experience in night vision, warfighter systems, optics, sensors, radios, or related defense technologies.
Strong experience translating customer requirements into technical specifications and product strategies.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex product initiatives without direct people management.
Eligible to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret Security Clearance; active clearance preferred.
Military experience or familiarity with dismounted soldier operations is highly desirable.
Able to prioritize tasks and drive projects to conclusion.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence across engineering, BD, and leadership.

Preferred Skills:

Deep technical understanding of imaging sensors, optical systems, radio technologies, and soldier‑network architectures.
Ability to integrate financial, technical, and market inputs into strategic recommendations.
Enjoys collaborative environments, relationship building, and mentoring early‑career product professionals.
Proven experience with customer‑facing engagements, requirement capture, and technical presentations.

configurations based on business requirements.

privileges across Jira and Confluence, including directory synchronization and access
governance.

preparation.

performance across teams.

users.

teams, and project stakeholders to implement Jira solutions that support Agile delivery and
organizational governance.

title: Resident Comfort Specialist
description:
Benefits:
  • 401(k)
  • Flexible schedule
  • Training & development
$18/hour | Flexible Schedule | Meaningful Work

Greetings everyone. My name is Claire. I am posting here today with the hopes of meeting six people. The people who can be described as people with heart and people with passion but more on that in a minute.

You see, there is a story behind my work and this post and here it goes.

I am an educator and former school principal turned nurse, turned nurse entrepreneur and geriatric wellness expert. Yes, education was my first love and my second love is nursing.

If you ask my mother, she would tell you that I have never met a stranger.

I was that girl who would go down the street to find someone to help and would stop and carry the groceries for the elderly neighbor and feed all the stray cats and lonely dogs that I could find.

During nursing school, I developed a true inquiring mind, and I could not sit still because I was pulled by various areas of health care. I worked in a long-term care community and I soon became pulled by the emotional and psychosocial needs of most older adults who live in long term care.

Many of them are sad and although they are amongst others, many feel lonely and left behind. I made myself a promise that I would take interest in those older adults and find a way to make them smile and feel happy even if it was just for a short time.

Through all my work seasons as a former teacher, a school principal, a nurse, a clinical chaplain, and now, a nurse entrepreneur, one truth has never changed: people need human connection.

That’s why I started this program — to bring kindness, laughter, and companionship to older adults in nursing homes and long-term care centers.


So, here is where you come in. I am in search of people with heart, and people with passion. I call these people Resident Comfort Specialists, and their job is simple yet life-changing: to bring joy and comfort to someone who feels forgotten. The job is very simple and very fulfilling.

As a Resident Comfort Specialist, you might spend your day with a resident doing any or all of the following:

  • Reading or telling stories
  • Watching a favorite TV show together
  • Singing along to old songs
  • Decorating a small tabletop Christmas tree
  • Or simply sitting beside someone who needs company
And yes — you’ll be paid $18 an hour for this beautiful work. It’s a job that fills your heart as much as your bank account.

All you need are three things:

  1. A degree in compassion. This is supposed to make your laugh because there is no degree in Compassion. You just need to be kind and gentle.
  2. A clean background check
  3. Your ID and Social Security number (so we can pay you!)
We’ll introduce you to the care team at the facility, guide you through the process, and help you start making a difference right away.

If you’ve been looking for work that truly means something — this is it.
You’ll be paid to make someone smile.
And you’ll go home knowing you helped another human being feel seen, valued, and loved.

Come join our team of compassionate companions.
We can’t wait to meet you.

Please respond with a good phone number and an email that you check regularly

Thanks and wishing you a beautiful week ahead.

TechnoPro IT is one of Japan's largest IT service companies, providing comprehensive IT solutions to clients nationwide.

With approximately 7,000 engineers across Japan, we support more than 900 client companies, primarily in the manufacturing industry, through infrastructure development, system integration, operation, and maintenance services.

As project demand continues to grow, we are actively seeking infrastructure engineers from around the world to join our team

Based on your experience, technical skills, and career goals, you will be assigned to infrastructure projects involving planning, design, implementation, operation, and maintenance.

Projects are primarily carried out at client sites or in collaboration with client teams


Project Examples

Cloud Infrastructure
  • Cloud architecture design and implementation using AWS and Azure

Network Infrastructure
  • Network planning, proposal, design, implementation, and operational design
  • Enterprise network operation and optimization
Server Infrastructure
  • Server design and implementation using virtualization technologies such as VMware and Hyper-V
  • Windows and Linux server administration, operation, and maintenance
Telecommunications & Mobile Networks
  • LTE and smartphone-related network deployment and operation

Scope of work may be changed based on business needs and company assignment policies


Working Environment

  • Approximately 7,000 engineers nationwide
  • More than 350 international engineers

Countries represented include:

South Korea, China, Myanmar, Vietnam, India, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Mongolia, Brazil, Nepal, France, Germany, and the United States.

    TechnoPro IT will assist you throughout the visa application process, from document preparation to entry into Japan.

  • Relocation Support
    We will arrange and provide your flight ticket to Japan upon joining the company.

  • Japanese Language Training Upon Joining
    New employees participate in a one-month Japanese language program, where they learn business Japanese and Japanese business culture.

  • Housing Assistance Program
    Company housing is available for employees. (Employee contribution starts from JPY 20,000 per month.)

  • Settlement Support in Japan
    We assist with essential procedures such as resident registration, opening a bank account, and other steps required to start daily life in Japan.

  • Ongoing Japanese Language Learning Support
    Employees may continue Japanese language training after joining, including courses designed to help achieve JLPT N1 certification.

With more than 350 international engineers working across Japan, we provide the support you need to build both your career and your life in Japan

Working Language

Japanese

Most projects require communication in Japanese.

Some projects may also require English communication skills.


Career Development

The average project assignment lasts approximately two years, allowing engineers to build a broad range of technical and project experience.

Depending on performance and aptitude, some employees take on leadership responsibilities within three to four years of joining the company.

We offer multiple career paths, including:

  • Infrastructure Specialist
  • Project Manager
  • IT Consultant
  • Technical Leader

We support career growth based on each employee's strengths and aspirations


Performance Evaluation

Performance evaluations are conducted annually.

Employees are evaluated based on technical performance, project contributions, professional development, and alignment with the company's values and code of conduct.

Main Responsibilities: Cloud migration, infrastructure design, implementation, and operations

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Windows or Linux server administration
  • Experience in network design, implementation, or operation

Knowledge/Skills/Competencies


Required Technical Skills

• Hands-on Engineering Tool Competency: Direct technical experience installing, patching, configuring, and deploying major EDA/CAD suites (such as Cadence, Synopsys, Ansys, or PTC).

• DevOps & Infrastructure Skills: Practical administrative experience managing Azure DevOps, Jira, Git repositories, CI/CD pipelines, and containerization systems (Docker/Kubernetes).

• License Architecture Knowledge: Functional knowledge of working with FlexLM, RMS, and similar vendor-specific license management server environments.

• Cross-Platform OS Familiarity: Technical comfort supporting Windows desktop applications alongside non-standard Linux base development images (Ubuntu, Rocky Linux) and enterprise endpoint configurations (BigFix, ThreatLocker).

Strongly Preferred Certifications

• CompTIA Linux+, Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA), or Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate

• Azure DevOps Engineer Expert or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional

• Certified Jira System Administrator

Soft Skills & Working Style

• Detailed Documentation: Proven ability to generate flawless application installation playbooks, precise packaging documentation, and clear troubleshooting scripts.

• Tactical Problem Solver: Exceptional technical troubleshooting skills, capable of identifying workarounds and diagnosing complex engineering application bugs within highly secure enterprise environments.

• Cross-functional Partner: Strong communication skills to interact directly and efficiently with HPS Design Center engineers, project managers, and global infrastructure tier-3 teams.

• Resource Optimization: Highly organized approach to tracking local software licensing utilization, preventing downtime, and advising management on upcoming software capacity or maintenance renewals.

Physical Demands

• Duties may require extended periods of sitting and sustained visual concentration on a computer monitor or on numbers and other detailed data. Repetitive manual movements (e.g., data entry, using a computer mouse, using a calculator, etc.) are frequently required.

title: Seasonal Store Cleaning & Operations Associate

Preferred

Essential Functions

Kohl’s may revise this job description at any time. To perform this job successfully, you must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily.   • Ability to perform the accountabilities listed in the “What You’ll Do” Section.

title: IT collaboration manager (Quản lý mảng vận hành ứng dụng tương tác )
description:
ĐỐI TÁC NGÂN HÀNG CỦA CHÚNG TÔI CẦN TUYỂN: IT collaboration manager (Quản lý mảng vận hành ứng dụng tương tác )
1. Quản lý tính sẵn sàng/Availability management

  • Đảm bảo các dịch vụ hạ tầng đáp ứng yêu cầu về tính sẵn sàng đã được cam kết
  • Cung cấp yêu cầu để đảm bảo các dịch vụ mới hoặc dịch vụ được sửa đổi / cập nhật đáp ứng yêu cầu về tính sẵn sàng đã được cam kết
  • Chủ động để duy trì, nâng cao tính sẵn sàng và sự ổn định của các dịch hạ tầng
  • Xây dựng và duy trì kế hoạch hoạt động liên tục cho các dịch vụ hạ tầng
  • Đảm bảo các sự cố liên quan đến hạ tầng được giải quyết
  • Đánh giá ảnh hưởng đến tính sẵn sàng của yêu cầu thay đổi mới
  • Tham gia vào ban tư vấn thay đổi - Change Advisory Board (CAB) nếu cần thiết
  • Chịu trách nhiệm giám sát tính sẵn sàng của dịch vụ hạ tầng, so sánh giữa thực tế và mục tiêu và giải quyết các thiếu sót
  • Phối hợp với các đơn vị khác đặc biệt là quản lý bảo mật và trung tâm giám sát hạ tầng và bảo mật
  • Vận hành, triển khai các giải pháp liên quan đến công nghệ hạ tầng
  • Thực hiện kiểm tra định kỳ về hạ tầng trong ngân hàng, lên kế hoạch và thực hiện các kế hoạch khắc phục khi cần
  • Quản lý các nhà cung cấp và giám sát chất lượng dịch vụ của các đối tác/ nhà cung cấp dịch vụ máy chủ và chịu trách nhiệm đối với các dịch vụ được cung cấp
  • Bảo trì, nâng cấp, tinh chỉnh thiết bị theo các yêu cầu của từng thời kỳ
  • Quản trị và triển khai các giải pháp bảo mật liên quan đến hạ tầng
  • Xây dựng danh mục công việc vận hành hàng ngày (checklist) và báo cáo hàng ngày kết quả và chất lượng của từng công việc

2. Quản lý tài sản /Asset management

  • Đảm bảo các tài sản được đồng nhất với quy ước đặt tên.
  • Đảm bảo tuân thủ các tiêu chuẩn nhận dạng cho các loại đối tượng, môi trường, vòng đời, phiên bản
  • Các thông tin của hệ thống được điều chỉnh phù hợp theo các yêu cầu thay đổi của từng thời kỳ
  • Duy trì danh mục tài sản bảo gồm loại thiết bị, địa chỉ IP, ngày đưa vào sử dụng, ngày hết bảo hành, ngày cần gia hạn bảo hành bảo trì
  • Duy trì danh mục các bản quyền, hợp đồng với các nhà cung cấp dịch vụ
  • Quản lý và duy trì hồ sơ hệ thống, thiết bị, các hệ thống ứng dụng được cài đặt trên máy chủ, mô hình triển khai, mô hình hoạt động và các thủ tục vận hành

3. Quản lý hiệu năng /Productivity management

  • Đảm bảo có đủ tài nguyên của hệ thống phục vụ cho các dịch vụ
  • Đảm bảo các quản lý CNTT nắm được nhu cầu sử dụng tài nguyên và xu hướng tăng trưởng
  • Cung cấp yêu cầu tài nguyên cho các dịch vụ CNTT được cập nhật hoặc mới bổ sung
  • Duy trì báo cáo chung cho hoạt động sử dụng hiệu năng của hạ tầng CNTT và xu hướng của nó
  • Đảm bảo kiểm tra hiệu năng được thực hiện cho các dịch vụ mới đưa vào vận hành
  • Chủ động nâng cao tính hiệu quả trọng việc sử dụng tài nguyên CNTT
  • Cung cấp và duy trì kế hoạch sử dụng tài nguyên
  • Đảm bảo các sự cố, vấn đề liên quan đến hiệu năng được giải quyết
  • Đánh giá ảnh hưởng đến hiệu năng của các yêu cầu thay đổi
  • Tham gia vào ban tư vấn thay đổi - Change Advisory Board (CAB) nếu cần thiết
  • Chịu trách nhiệm giám sát mức độ sử dụng tài nguyên, so sánh giữa nhu cầu thực tế và kế hoạch và giải quyết các vấn đề liên quan đến tài nguyên

4. Quản lý thay đổi /Change management

  • Cung cấp đánh giá kịp thời về một thay đổi được thực thi ảnh hưởng
  • đến hạ tầng và các dịch vụ
  • Truyền thông bất kỳ vấn đề gây ra bởi thay đổi đến người yêu cầu và người thực hiện
  • Cập nhật hướng dẫn vận hành nếu cần thiết
  • Giám sát chặt chẽ tiến trình thực hiện các thay đổi
  • Cập nhật trạng thái thay đổi
  • Chịu trách nhiệm chuẩn hóa thiết kế hạ tầng máy chủ

5. Quản lý cấu hình /Configuration management

  • Chịu trách nhiệm về tiêu chuẩn thiết bị theo từng thời kỳ
  • Chịu trách nhiệm chuẩn hóa và duy trì tiêu chuẩn hệ điều hành, danh mục phần mềm và phiên bản liên quan theo từng thời kỳ
  • Chịu trách nhiệm quản lý, duy trì và cập nhật hệ thống quản lý cấu hình (CMS)
  • Chịu trách nhiệm sao lưu cấu hình thiết bị máy chủ

6. Quản lý sự kiện /Event Management

  • Chịu trách nhiệm thực hiện các công việc quản lý giám sát các hệ thống hạ tầng cũng như toàn bộ các hệ thống ứng dụng dịch vụ CNTT
  • Đảm bảo tất cả các hệ thống hạ tầng và dịch vụ của Khối CNTT được giám sát
  • Chịu trách nhiệm quản lý vòng đời của mọi sự cố CNTT
  • Đảm bảo xử lý kịp thời các sự kiện để duy trì SLAs đã được cam kết

7. Quản lý chất lượng dịch vụ /Service Quality Management

  • Vận hành và duy trì các dịch vụ CNTT
  • Phối hợp với các đơn vị khác để điều tra, đánh giá, xử lý các sự cố cũng như xác định xu hướng tích/tiêu cực và các sự cố được xác định và giải quyết. Đưa ra các hành động khắc phục
  • Đảm bảo rằng các phân tích sâu được thực hiện để xác định nguyên nhân gốc của các xu hướng tiêu cực
  • Phân tích, báo cáo về xu hướng về hiệu năng và ảnh hưởng do các vấn đề CNTT gây ra
  • Đảm bảo các dịch vụ CNTT được vận hành trong SLAs được cam kết
  • Phân tích các dữ liệu đã được thu thập

8. Quản lý nguồn lực /Human Resource management

  • Chủ động phân bổ nguồn lực để hỗ trợ các công việc vận hành hàng ngày cũng như các dự án
  • Cung cấp nhân sự và kế hoạch để vận hành trung tâm giám sát hạ tầng và bảo mật
  • Quản lý, duy trì và giám sát danh mục hoạt động trong nội bộ trung tâm vận hành (IT Operation Porfolio)

Requirements

title: Licensed Preventive Supervisor
description:
PURPOSE:
The purpose of the Staten Island Family Services – Juvenile Justice Initiative program in Preventive Service Department is to provide support for families with child(ren) (ages 0 to 17) The Preventive Services Department provides child welfare services using Evidence Based models to ensure that families are able to provide safe environments for their children, keep children safe in their homes and reduce the need for foster care. Prevention is an essential part of the child welfare continuum and requires a commitment to the wellbeing of all members of a client family. All services are provided in a family’s home and community.

POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Licensed Preventive Social Worker Supervisor has full responsibility for the on-going clinical guidance of the clinical/case planner staff members. The Supervisor also provides on-going training and supervision for the clinical staff. The Supervisor may be called upon to perform any of the line functions normally performed by a social worker/case planner and is expected to be fully proficient in those areas. The Supervisor is familiar with all Preventive Service and Child Welfare Standards and functions as an internal resource on such matters.

KEY ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Provides regularly scheduled weekly supervision to all clinical/case planning staff members.
Evaluates appropriateness of service plans (FASPs) and approves these based upon an understanding of any safety/risk concerns in the family and the service needs of the children and parents.
Facilitates weekly clinical case conference as well as Family Team Conferences
Completes job performance evaluations and provides professional development support on a regular basis.
May supervise student interns.
Responsible for intake on new referrals.
Provides frequent and appropriate feedback to program stakeholders including ACS Child Protection
Understand ACS/OCFS electronic systems including PROMIS and CNNX
Provides all necessary notes, progress notes, other paperwork as required by ACS and JBFCS including entering monthly supervisory notes in CNNX for CWS cases and in the case record for ADVPO cases.
Cover for Director in his/her absence
Work a hybrid schedule based on program needs
Complete agency internal Incident Reports in Alltrac system.
Participating in Family Team Conferences (FTCs)
Other duties as assigned

CORE COMPETENCIES:

Basic social work knowledge and understanding of stages of change
Ability to provide in-home therapy and child welfare services
Ability to establish a strong therapeutic relationship with families.
Understanding of the use of family therapy principles to provide services
Understanding of early childhood development and related theories and models of practice
Strong Assessment skills to evaluate dynamics and interactions within the family

Ability to Implement strategies to improve family communication and support

EDUCATIONAL/TRAINING REQUIRED:

Master’s degree in social work, Psychology, Mental Health Counseling, Marriage and Family Therapy, Creative Arts Therapy or a related subject area.

EXPERIENCE REQUIRED/LANGUAGE PREFERENCE:

Minimum of three years of related experience in Child Welfare and/or Family Therapy.
Specialized experience with specific client population or specialty (domestic violence, substance abuse, community outreach, etc.) preferred.

COMPUTER SKILLS REQUIRED:

Knowledge of Microsoft office required
Knowledge and experience with the Connections system preferred

VISUAL AND MANUAL DEXIERITY:

Limited applications of manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination

title: Resident Comfort Specialist
description:
Benefits:
  • 401(k)
  • Flexible schedule
  • Opportunity for advancement
$18/hour | Flexible Schedule | Meaningful Work

Greetings everyone. My name is Claire. I am posting here today with the hopes of meeting six people. The people who can be described as people with heart and people with passion but more on that in a minute.

You see, there is a story behind my work and this post and here it goes.

I am an educator and former school principal turned nurse, turned nurse entrepreneur and geriatric wellness expert. Yes, education was my first love and my second love is nursing.

If you ask my mother, she would tell you that I have never met a stranger.

I was that girl who would go down the street to find someone to help and would stop and carry the groceries for the elderly neighbor and feed all the stray cats and lonely dogs that I could find.

During nursing school, I developed a true inquiring mind, and I could not sit still because I was pulled by various areas of health care. I worked in a long-term care community and I soon became pulled by the emotional and psychosocial needs of most older adults who live in long term care.

Many of them are sad and although they are amongst others, many feel lonely and left behind. I made myself a promise that I would take interest in those older adults and find a way to make them smile and feel happy even if it was just for a short time.

Through all my work seasons as a former teacher, a school principal, a nurse, a clinical chaplain, and now, a nurse entrepreneur, one truth has never changed: people need human connection.

That’s why I started this program — to bring kindness, laughter, and companionship to older adults in nursing homes and long-term care centers.


So, here is where you come in. I am in search of people with heart, and people with passion. I call these people Resident Comfort Specialists, and their job is simple yet life-changing: to bring joy and comfort to someone who feels forgotten. The job is very simple and very fulfilling.

As a Resident Comfort Specialist, you might spend your day with a resident doing any or all of the following:

  • Reading or telling stories
  • Watching a favorite TV show together
  • Singing along to old songs
  • Decorating a small tabletop Christmas tree
  • Or simply sitting beside someone who needs company
And yes — you’ll be paid $18 an hour for this beautiful work. It’s a job that fills your heart as much as your bank account.

All you need are three things:

  1. A degree in compassion. This is supposed to make your laugh because there is no degree in Compassion. You just need to be kind and gentle.
  2. A clean background check
  3. Your ID and Social Security number (so we can pay you!)
We’ll introduce you to the care team at the facility, guide you through the process, and help you start making a difference right away.

If you’ve been looking for work that truly means something — this is it.
You’ll be paid to make someone smile.
And you’ll go home knowing you helped another human being feel seen, valued, and loved.

Come join our team of compassionate companions.
We can’t wait to meet you.

Please respond with a good phone number and an email that you check regularly

Thanks and wishing you a beautiful week ahead.

Ability to take coaching well and communicate respectfully with others to ensure and promote a positive teamwork culture.

title: Reservoir Engineer/Advisor/Manager
description:
The Reservoir candidate will help convert subsurface understanding into free cash flow generation from Marcellus and Utica unconventional shale assets as part of the Reservoir and Asset Management team. Primary responsibilities include reservoir analysis and well performance evaluation, type curve and decline model development, DCA/RTA/PTA/DFIT interpretation, spacing and completion optimization, economic evaluation, field development planning, and support of the annual SEC-compliant reserves process. The Reservoir candidate works closely with geology, land, operations, midstream, finance, and corporate reserves. The candidate must be flexible, detail-oriented, ambitious, self-starter and prepared to work for an organization with a large and diverse asset base.
Note: Depending on the candidate’s qualifications and experience, this position may be filled at the Senior Engineer, Advisor, or Manager level; higher levels carry broader technical leadership and, at the Manager level, responsibility for leading and developing the reservoir engineering team.
Target Responsibilities:

  • Perform decline curve analysis, rate transient analysis, pressure transient analysis, DFIT interpretation, and other reservoir engineering techniques to evaluate performance; translate findings into spacing, completion stage design, and production management guidance to maximize free cash flow.• Perform economic analysis, sensitivities, and capital ranking, including quality control.• Develop, maintain, and apply type curves, decline models, and economic evaluations consistent with forecast methodology, reserves controls, and technical standards.• Support integrated development planning for Marcellus and Utica assets, including inventory life, development pacing, portfolio optimization, and capital ranking.• Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to integrate geologic, geophysical, and petrophysical data into reservoir models.• Analyze the effects of pressure dependent permeability on ultimate recovery; optimize drawdown strategy based on pricing environment.• Evaluate parent/child interaction and frac-hit impacts, and recommend mitigation strategies, lateral spacing, and landing targets.• Integrate geological, geophysical, operational, and financial data into reserves and resource assessments.• Develop and update reservoir models, leverage simulation and analytics, to support production forecasting, reserve estimation, and decision-making.• Support the annual SEC-compliant reserves process, including Year-end Reserves reporting, third-party audit communication, quarterly reconciliations, and reserves-based lending engineering reviews, with reserves classifications aligned to SEC regulations, SPE-PRMS, and internal governance standards.• Benchmark well and asset performance against internal metrics and peer operators.• Work with broader team using available public/private data to determine land acquisition targets for future development, and provide technical diligence on A&D opportunities, inventory quality, and commercial fit.• Work closely with field operations teams to optimize well completions and production strategies.• Utilize data analytics platforms, such as Spotfire, to analyze large datasets and identify trends, correlations, and opportunities for improvement in well performance.• Provide technical guidance and mentorship to less experienced engineers and geoscientists.• Stay up to date with industry advancements, best practices, and emerging technologies relevant to reservoir engineering.

Minimum Requirements:

  • B.S. in Engineering (Petroleum or related)• Minimum of 5 years of E&P reservoir engineering experience with a focus on unconventional shale gas.• Working knowledge of (demonstrated expertise expected at the Advisor and Manager levels):o Type curve creation, DCA, RTA, PTA, DFIT design/interpretation.o Shale development: spacing/stacking, parent/child risk mitigation, frac-hit diagnostics, landing target selection, completion optimization.o Economic evaluation, cashflow fundamentals (operating cashflow, rate of return, DCF and related investment metrics), sensitivity analysis, and capital ranking frameworks.o Reserves processes (SEC/PRMS), year-end bookings, and auditor engagement.• Proficient in MS Suite, Harmony, & ARIES with understanding of databases (SQL, Oracle, Access).• Working knowledge of unconventional development, production, and midstream operations, and understanding of upstream, midstream, and A&D workflows for asset evaluation and management.• Strong knowledge of reservoir characterization, production forecasting, and reserve estimation techniques.• Experience with data analytics platforms like Spotfire and PowerBI for data analysis and visualization.• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to make sound engineering decisions based on data.• Strong team and relationship building skills, with excellent verbal and written communication and the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams.• Ability to coach and mentor less experienced staff.• Proven ability to manage multiple projects and prioritize tasks in a fast-paced environment.• Strong commitment to safety and environmental stewardship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior Marcellus/Utica experience.• Advanced degree in engineering.• Experience in technical leadership or people management, including developing and evaluating technical staff.• Familiarity with reserves governance frameworks and internal controls required of public companies (SOX, audit processes).• Working knowledge of Enersight.• Experience with ARIES Economics Software.• Experience with SAP.• Experience with Peloton.• Experience with Enverus.• Familiarity with midstream interfaces, compression strategy, and line pressure impacts.• Knowledge of facilities and production operation constraints relevant to dry/residue gas systems.• Professional Engineering License.
